From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC workload intake & benchmarking hypotheses

Hi Maya / team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while we scope the POC. This thread will capture the workload inputs we discussed plus our benchmarking hypotheses and ownership.

1) High-level goals (what success looks like)
- Deliver a 2-week trial that demonstrates stable 99th percentile latency under your peak workload and keeps per-response token cost below ~$0.006 (as an example gating metric).
- Verify fidelity on your two core flows: transaction enrichment (short prompts) and claim summarization (longer context).

2) Workload profile (what we need from you) — please confirm or correct:
- Endpoint a) enrichment: expected baseline RPS 15, concurrency 30, typical prompt length 30-80 tokens, average response 40 tokens. Burst window: spikes to 100 RPS for ~120s during business hours.
- Endpoint b) summarization: baseline RPS 2, concurrency 5, prompt lengths 800-2,000 tokens (full claim + metadata), responses ~150-400 tokens. Bursts up to 12 RPS for 60–180s when heavy ingestion occurs.
- Day-of-week pattern: weekday peaks, minimal traffic overnight.

3) Hypotheses we will validate in the POC
- Continuous batching will reduce per-token cost for the enrichment flow without violating the 200ms p50 latency target.
- Long-context summarization will require KV-cache tuning and a 16GB token cache profile to avoid repeated recomputation.
- Under burst conditions, graceful degradation via route fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant will keep 95th p99 latency within the SLA while preserving quality.

4) Roles / owners
- Redwood: Soojin (sales lead, scope/acceptance), Ben (CS/ops - runbook & benchmark execution), Vivek (solutions architect - runtime config & kernel tuning).
- EverLedger: Maya (CTO - technical signoff), Ops Lead (POC execution point-of-contact).

5) Immediate next steps (action items)
- Maya / Ops: share representative sample payloads (JSON) for both flows, and a short traffic trace for a typical weekday (CSV or timeline). — due Tue 2027-06-15
- Redwood: produce a POC runbook with benchmark cases (RPS/concurrency/burst scenarios) and a success-criteria spreadsheet. — will share by Mon 2027-06-14
- Schedule a 60-min kick-off with Ben + Vivek to walk the runbook. Proposed: Wed 2027-06-16 10:00 PT.

Attachments: please upload a sample payload set and any retention/PII constraints. I attached a template payload file for your convenience.

Thanks — looking forward to the kick-off.

—
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — good summary. Quick clarifications and I've attached a small sample set (10 enrichment requests + 3 long summaries) and a 24h traffic CSV.

Corrections to workload:
- Enrichment baseline is likely closer to 22 RPS (not 15) during morning peak; concurrency target should be 40. Bursts can hit 180 RPS for up to 3 minutes (we usually see 2–3 short spikes).
- Summarization prompts are typically 600–1,800 tokens; average response ~220 tokens. We can trim docs but want the model to see full claims for evaluation.

Constraints:
- All POC logs must scrub PII. We can provide masked payloads; do not send raw data off our VPC.
- Procurement will need the trial duration and sample SLA stated for internal approvals (we prefer a 4-week window but happy to start with 2 weeks if we can extend).

We'll upload the sample files to the shared Drive link you provided and label them EV-4821/sample-inputs.

Maya

Looping in ops/arch notes and the proposed benchmark matrix. Short notes:

- We'll run three benchmark passes:
  A) Baseline steady-state (72h synthetic run matching daytime profile at 80% baseline RPS)
  B) Burst probe (multiple 3-minute spikes up to 200 RPS for enrichment flow; 180s bursts for summarization up to 12 RPS)
  C) Long-run tail check (4-hour run to validate p99 / KV cache stability for summarization).

- Data handling: we will only use the masked payloads you provide and run in Redwood Dedicated trial tenancy. Logs will be redacted per your PII guidance; we'll supply an audit snapshot for your team.

- Request for tickets/artefacts from EverLedger to make the run deterministic:
  * A typical 24h traffic CSV (you mentioned you'll upload).
  * Sample tokenization report (if you have a tokenizer mapping) — helps with token-length distributions.
  * Any custom post-processing (scoring/scaffold) hooks that you run client-side so we can mirror latency.

Action: Soojin — can you confirm preferred kick-off time and I'll circulate the Redwood runbook (draft) plus a Google Sheet with the benchmark cases and acceptance gates?

Ben
